_what: SCOPE MEASUREMENT for the ground-up rebuild — what actually changes under the current chain, measured per level BEFORE the rebuild rather than discovered during it.
why: The 77-member corpus was built across SIX code eras (july31 5b48421; aug06/aug09 a mix of 82f67f8, f43e482, a1dc91b, 1791bb4, 3f1980d; aug14 e8aab41). Nobody had shown those eras agree. A full from-raws rebuild was proposed to make provenance uniform; this measured whether it was REPAIR or VERIFICATION first.

era_equivalence.result: SIX OF SEVEN ERAS ARE MEASURED EQUIVALENT. THE SEVENTH IS A CODE-PATH ARGUMENT, NOT A MEASUREMENT — this field previously said 'ALL SIX ERAS ... Proven above', which was wrong on BOTH counts and is corrected here.
era_equivalence.positive_control: one pixel +0.01 -> 1 differing, max 0.01 — the comparison resolves a single pixel
era_equivalence.reading: the heterogeneous PIPEREV stamps are a LABELLING inconsistency, not a data one. A from-raws rebuild would reproduce these members exactly, at ~13 h, and buys a uniform stamp rather than a corrected pixel.
era_equivalence.era_count_correction: There are SEVEN eras across the 77 members, not six: e8aab41 x25 (all aug14), 5b48421 x17, f43e482 x14, 82f67f8 x10, a1dc91b x6, 1791bb4 x3, 3f1980d x2. The three tests below cover six of them. e8aab41 — the LARGEST at 25 of 77 members, 32% — is NOT among them.
era_equivalence.how_the_seventh_closes: MECHANISM, not measurement: every member-building script is UNCHANGED between e8aab41 and HEAD — run_undistort_groups.sh, run_undistort_pipeline.sh, calibrate_light.sh, build_master_dark.sh, build_sky_flat.sh, stack_rejection.sh, install_lens_model.sh, siril_run.sh. stamp_headers.sh IS sourced by the groups builder and DID change, so it was checked specifically: the builder calls header_registration_lines with two args and the additions are guarded on a third, so member headers are unaffected. That is a sound argument and it is NOT the same evidence as a pixel comparison. Recorded as MECHANISM so a later reader does not quote it as measured.

what_the_current_chain_actually_changes.members: NOTHING — calibrate/warp/register/reject were not touched by the unit. Proven above.
what_the_current_chain_actually_changes.per_set_stacks: PIXELS UNCHANGED — composed by run_undistort_groups' own inline star-pair compose (final.ssf), NOT by run_undistort_compose, so the --ref work does not reach them. They gain SOLVCENT/SOLVMAXS at render.
what_the_current_chain_actually_changes.night_combines: PIXELS IDENTICAL — MEASURED: aug14's 25-member night recomposed under the current chain gives 0 differing of 124,943,751, same 7977x5221 canvas. The --ref derivation STANDS DOWN on a single night by design ('single night — AUTO is harmless'), so only the REGREF stamp is added (auto, index 1).
what_the_current_chain_actually_changes.corpus_combine: THE ONLY PIXEL CHANGE. Multi-night, so the derivation FIRES: canvas 8515x5666 -> 8540x5685, +0.63% area, same sky, REGREF=36:aug09/groups_set-02/sub_02.fit REGREFSR=derived. Plus the coverage rung makes its solve confident (was NO SOLUTION at the shipped invocation, now logodds 112).

rebuild_plan_predictions._note: pre-registered so a deviation is a FINDING rather than a surprise
rebuild_plan_predictions.per_set_renders: pixel-identical products; new SOLVCENT/SOLVMAXS keys only
rebuild_plan_predictions.corpus: canvas +0.63%, confident solve, derived reference — a DECLARED DELTA, and the baseline must be re-seeded when it is accepted

WITHDRAWN_CLAIM_uniform_stamp: This record previously said a from-raws rebuild 'buys a uniform stamp rather than a corrected pixel'. IT BUYS NEITHER. MEASURED: a composite's PIPEREV is INHERITED FROM ITS REGISTRATION REFERENCE MEMBER, not from the code that built it. Old corpus PIPEREV 5b48421 = its reference member 1's; new corpus PIPEREV 1791bb4 = its reference member 36's; HEAD when the new one was built was 9106bc4 — neither. siril's `stack` propagates the reference member's header and stamp_headers.sh's composite KEYS tuple does not list PIPEREV, so nothing overrides it. No rebuild could make a composite's stamp uniform, because the stamp is not the building code's. See datasets/corpus/piperev_inheritance.json.
